item.title: Fenland students prepare for national skills competition
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Fenland students prepare for national skills competition
Students from across the Fens have been recognised at a special event ahead of the WorldSkills UK national finals. Learners from March, Terrington St John, and Wisbech are among those representing the College of West Anglia in the competition, often described as the skills Olympics.
The celebration at the King’s Lynn campus honoured students who progressed through regional heats to reach the finals this November. Local competitors include Erika Rimkus, Finn Mcauley, and Paige Marshall from Wisbech, Marc Watson from March, and Rianna Moore from Terrington St John. College principal David Pomfret praised the finalists, noting that they represent the top five percent of entrants in their respective vocational fields.

item.title: Looking back at October community events in the Fens
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Looking back at October community events in the Fens
We are taking a look back at community highlights from across the region during past Octobers. In 2017, King’s Lynn hosted a Halloween Spooktacular at the Vancouver Quarter, while young artists were celebrated at Gaywood Library’s superhero drawing competition. That same year, a 24-hour spinathon at Lynnsport raised over one thousand pounds for the British Heart Foundation.
Looking further back to 2013, the Railway Arms in Downham Market was named the national cider pub of the year. Meanwhile, in Swaffham, the cemetery chapel was rededicated following a forty-five thousand pound renovation. These stories reflect a busy period of local activity, from charity fundraising and remembrance services to community celebrations held across our towns.

item.title: King’s Lynn ambulance station hosts stem cell donor event
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn ambulance station hosts stem cell donor event
Staff and volunteers at the King’s Lynn ambulance station are holding a stem cell swabbing event this Monday. The initiative aims to find a donor for Reuben, the ten-month-old son of a local paramedic, who was recently diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia. The East of England Ambulance Service is hosting the session to encourage more people to join the DKMS stem cell register.
Those aged between 16 and 55 can participate in the simple cheek swab test. Members of the public who are unable to attend the station can also support the appeal by requesting a home testing kit through the DKMS website. Every new registration increases the potential for finding a life-saving match for patients in need of a transplant.

item.title: Wisbech college hosts event to encourage young women into STEM careers
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Wisbech college hosts event to encourage young women into STEM careers
Students from across the Fens have attended a special event at the College of West Anglia’s Green Skills Academy in Wisbech. The "Girls in STEM" day aimed to inspire young women to consider careers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics.
Pupils from Thomas Clarkson Academy in Wisbech and Neale-Wade Academy in March joined college students for practical activities, including virtual welding and thermal imaging. Representatives from various industries, including Anglian Water and Polypipe, were on hand to discuss career pathways. Organisers say the event was designed to challenge traditional gender stereotypes and highlight the growing need for a diverse workforce in sectors supporting a greener economy.

item.title: Nine new bus shelters installed across King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Nine new bus shelters installed across King’s Lynn
Nine new bus shelters have been installed in and around King’s Lynn following an £82,500 replacement programme. The project, funded by West Norfolk Council and a Norfolk County Council grant, replaces ageing structures that had suffered from damage and structural issues.
New shelters are now located on Winston Churchill Drive, William Booth Road, Gayton Road, Saddlebow Road, Queen Mary Road, and Parkway. Officials say the modern replacements are expected to last for 25 years. By removing advertising and electrical connections from the previous sites, the council expects to recoup its investment within four and a half years.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Free electrical safety checks available in King’s Lynn
Residents are invited to have their heated blankets, throws, and portable heaters tested for safety next month. Norfolk County Council Trading Standards and the Norfolk Fire and Rescue Service are hosting a drop-in event at King’s Lynn Library on Monday, November 2. Experts will be on hand between 10am and noon to test items and provide advice on fire safety and scam prevention.
Last year, 60 percent of items brought to similar sessions failed safety checks. Residents are encouraged to bring items belonging to friends or neighbours who cannot attend. No booking is required for the session at the New Conduit Street library, and the service is free of charge.

The Rotary Club of King’s Lynn has promised to support a refurbishment project at the Mr Bee’s Family Centre. The pledge follows a presentation by Abbie Mulcairn from the charity Brave Futures, which provides specialist support to children and young people across Norfolk and Suffolk who have experienced sexual abuse.
During the meeting, the charity highlighted that referrals at their King’s Lynn centre have more than doubled over the past six months. Rotary club members heard that the organisation is currently managing high demand while navigating challenges within the criminal justice system. The club president confirmed they will assist with the planned improvements to the centre’s therapy room.

Harding’s Pits in South Lynn granted village green status
A long-running campaign to protect Harding’s Pits in South Lynn has reached a successful conclusion. Norfolk County Council has officially approved the site for village green status, following a proposal submitted by West Norfolk Council earlier this year.
The designation provides statutory protection against development and encroachment, ensuring the land remains available for community use. This decision marks the end of a process spanning more than 30 years, which began with an initial application by the Lynn 2,000 lobby group. Local campaigners and councillors have welcomed the news, noting that the status will safeguard the area’s natural habitats and public open space for future generations.

item.title: King’s Lynn students design new logo for local educational charity
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn students design new logo for local educational charity
Graphic design students from the College of West Anglia have been recognised for their work on a new logo challenge. Armanda Rakstys, Chloe Wilson, and Kian Moon were tasked with creating a visual identity for the West Norfolk and King’s Lynn Girls’ Schools Trust. The project required the Level 3 students to reflect the charity’s history and its commitment to supporting education for girls and young women in the region.
The trust, which was established in 1983, manages funds from the former West Norfolk and King’s Lynn High School for Girls. College staff and trust representatives praised the students for their research, professionalism, and creative approach to the brief.

East Cambridgeshire District Council seeks devolution pilot
East Cambridgeshire District Council is challenging plans for Local Government Reorganisation. The authority has formally called for a devolution pilot to be introduced instead. The move comes as the council seeks to address proposed changes to local administrative structures. No further details regarding the timeline or the specific nature of the pilot scheme have been released at this stage.
